register.name: Eurobond of the Government of Georgia, coupon 5.125%
register.detail: Ministry of Finance of Georgia · listed on the London Stock Exchange · announced 29 January 2026 · coupon 5.125% · orders of US$2.8 billion from more than 100 investors · refinances the 2021 Eurobonds
register.note: Investor demand reached a record US$2.8 billion, about 5.5 times the amount offered, as the Ministry of Finance states
register.text: A US$500 million Eurobond of the Government of Georgia, listed on the London Stock Exchange with a coupon of 5.125%, whose proceeds refinance the Eurobonds issued in 2021. The Ministry of Finance states that the coupon is the lowest among Eurobonds issued in the past four years by countries with a credit rating comparable to Georgia’s, and that the country’s risk level fell by more than 50 basis points.

register.name: Commercial Bank Resolution Preparedness Project
register.detail: World Bank (IBRD) · loan agreement signed 30 July 2026 by the Minister of Finance and the World Bank Regional Director for the South Caucasus · contingent credit line for the Resolution Fund
register.note: Available only on an event defined by law, when the National Bank of Georgia places a commercial bank into resolution
register.text: An IBRD loan of US$35 million in contingent financing for Georgia’s Resolution Fund, to finance the resolution of a commercial bank should one be needed. The National Bank of Georgia states that the funds are not intended for use under normal circumstances and are a further safeguard until the Fund reaches its target of 3 percent of insured deposits, a protection for the savings and credit of households and firms.

register.name: Trans-Caspian Transport Corridor: Georgia Accessibility and Transport Enhancement
register.detail: World Bank · approved 2 June 2026 · total project cost over US$750 million, co-financed by AIIB and ADB · JSC Georgian Railway and roads in Kakheti
register.note: Expected: 95% availability of locomotives, a 20% rise in railway revenue and about 43 minutes cut from the Telavi–Poti journey
register.text: World Bank Group financing of US$372 million for new energy-efficient electric locomotives and the efficiency, finances and governance of JSC Georgian Railway, two four-lane road segments in Kakheti (Badiauri–Chalaubani–Bakurtsikhe), a road from Gurjaani to Telavi and the digitisation of road asset management. It also supports women entrepreneurs in Kakheti, which serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Enhancing Energy Security through Power Interconnection and Renewable Energy (ESPIRE) Program, Phase 1
register.detail: World Bank (IBRD) · approved 21 May 2024 · P179950 · first phase of a multiphase programme
register.note: Preparation of the Black Sea Submarine Cable: the corridor, seabed surveys and coordination between governments
register.text: An IBRD loan of US$35 million for the first phase of the ESPIRE Program: identifying a corridor for the Black Sea Submarine Cable, geophysical and geotechnical surveys of the seabed, and technical assistance for coordination between the participating governments. If the cable proceeds, later phases would strengthen the grid on land and help finance the cable with other financiers; it serves the energy standard.

register.name: Trans-Caspian Corridor: Georgia Accessibility and Transport Enhancement Project (AIIB co-financing)
register.detail: AIIB · sovereign · financing approved 15 September 2026 · co-financed with the World Bank, the lead co-financier, at equal shares, pari passu
register.note: Co-finances the road connectivity component (US$336 million) and the road-sector components of the project led by the World Bank
register.text: AIIB sovereign financing of US$181.07 million for the Trans-Caspian corridor project led by the World Bank, co-financing at equal shares the road connectivity component of US$336 million and the components for road-sector institutions. The World Bank states that AIIB and ADB co-finance the remainder of a project whose total cost is over US$750 million.

register.name: Tbilisi Bypass Project (Lots 4 and 5)
register.detail: ADB · approved, news release of 30 July 2026 · 18.9 km, four lanes · Tbilisi Airport–Lochini and Lochini–Rustavi, with access and service roads
register.note: Upgrades part of the East–West Highway around the capital
register.text: An ADB loan of US$250 million to build an 18.9-kilometre, four-lane section of a highway bypassing Tbilisi, from Tbilisi Airport to Lochini and from Lochini to Rustavi, upgrading part of the East–West Highway. ADB expects it to ease congestion and improve the reliability of freight.

register.name: Clean, Local, Equitable Access to Reliable Water Program (CLEAR)
register.detail: ADB · approved 24 October 2025 · results-based loan · at least 100 rural settlements
register.note: Climate- and disaster-resilient rural water supply, with new operation and maintenance rules using digital tools
register.text: An ADB results-based loan of US$233.2 million to expand and rehabilitate water supply infrastructure in at least 100 rural settlements, for a continuous and reliable supply of safe drinking water. It serves the water standard, where 70.5% of Georgians have safely managed drinking water, and eases the household burden on women.

register.name: Batumi–Sarpi Road
register.detail: ADB · approved 26 September 2025 · 11 km to trans-European motorway standards · the final section of the East–West Highway, to the border with Türkiye at Sarpi
register.note: With slope stabilisation, rockfall protection and 500 metres of Black Sea shoreline protection
register.text: An ADB loan of US$360 million for a new climate-resilient road from the Batumi bypass to the border with Türkiye at Sarpi, the final section of Georgia’s East–West Highway. It also funds a modern road asset management system, road safety awareness and equipment for a bridge-testing laboratory at the Georgian Technical University.

register.name: Energy Storage and Green Hydrogen Development Project
register.detail: ADB · approved 16 April 2025 · 200 MW/200 MWh battery energy storage system at the Ksani substation near Tbilisi · implemented by Georgian State Electrosystem
register.note: With a US$400,000 technical assistance grant for the development of green hydrogen
register.text: An ADB loan of US$104 million to add a 200 MW/200 MWh battery energy storage system to the transmission network at the Ksani substation near Tbilisi, to strengthen Georgia’s energy security. A US$400,000 technical assistance grant supports the development of green hydrogen from surplus power in the peak seasons; it serves the energy standard.

register.name: Modern Skills for Better Jobs, Subprogram 2
register.detail: ADB · approved 22 November 2024 · policy-based loan of GEL 68,198,000 (about US$25 million) · ADB’s first local currency sovereign loan in Georgia
register.note: Vocational education and training, including courses at general schools in regions without colleges
register.text: An ADB policy-based loan in lari to improve the quality, relevance and reach of vocational education and training, bring private firms into the design of programmes and offer vocational training at general education schools in regions without colleges, for rural and disadvantaged young people. It serves the education and livelihood standards and the government’s aim of more public debt in lari.

register.name: Pharmaceutical logistics, Aversi Pharma
register.detail: EBRD · announced 6 June 2026 · loan of up to €10M · new central warehouse in Tbilisi
register.note: Renovation and automation of a newly acquired central warehouse
register.text: An EBRD loan of up to €10 million to Aversi Pharma, one of Georgia’s leading pharmaceutical and healthcare companies, which runs one of the country’s largest pharmacy chains, to renovate and automate a newly acquired central warehouse in Tbilisi. It serves the health standard through the supply of medicines.

register.name: Medium-term finance for small businesses, Credo Bank
register.detail: EBRD · announced 4 June 2026 · loan of up to US$40M (€34.6M) · at least 45% on-lent to women-led and women-owned businesses
register.note: For micro, small and medium-sized enterprises across Georgia, with a focus on the regions
register.text: An EBRD loan of up to US$40 million to Credo Bank to widen access to medium-term finance for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises across Georgia, with a focus on the regions, where affordable medium-term finance in lari is limited. At least 45 per cent is to be on-lent to women-led and women-owned businesses; it serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Small business, women-led and green lending in lari, TBC Bank
register.detail: ADB · news release of 26 January 2026 · GEL 270M (about US$100M) to JSC TBC Bank · up to 70% for MSMEs, at least 20% of that for women-owned and women-led firms · at least 30% for green investments
register.note: Green investments are to meet the green taxonomy of the National Bank of Georgia
register.text: An ADB loan in lari of GEL 270 million (about US$100 million) to TBC Bank, for stable, affordable and longer-tenor loans to micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, at least a fifth of them for women-owned and women-led firms. At least 30% is to finance green investments that meet the National Bank of Georgia’s green taxonomy; it serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Supporting inclusion through microfinance, Microbank Crystal
register.detail: Council of Europe Development Bank · approved 13 June 2025 · programme loan · Crystal adds 50% for a portfolio of €16M (Crystal, 15 August 2025)
register.note: For micro-entrepreneurs, women entrepreneurs and smallholder farmers with limited or no access to traditional banks
register.text: A CEB programme loan to JSC Microbank Crystal for micro-entrepreneurs and microenterprises, including women entrepreneurs and smallholder farmers, with limited or no access to the traditional banking system. It finances working capital and fixed investment, including agricultural investments, to keep jobs and support self-employment; it serves the livelihood standard.

items.text: More than four fifths of the power from mountain rivers.

items.text: Georgians abroad send home more than a tenth of the economy.

items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.

items.text: Tbilisi, the Caucasus and its vineyards: visitors from every continent.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 20.5% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: Georgian Wheelchair Workshop
items.text: A Tbilisi social enterprise that makes all-terrain, urban, lightweight and bariatric wheelchairs fitted to each user, with ramps and transfer lifts, employing people with disabilities alongside other staff; a WHO report of 2025 names it the only local wheelchair manufacturer in Georgia.

items.name: Microbank Crystal
items.text: A Georgian microbank with 27 years in microlending, licensed by the National Bank of Georgia in February 2025, that lends to micro, small and medium-sized and women-led businesses and serves more than 100,000 people through 48 branches.

items.name: Babale
items.text: A social enterprise in Tbilisi, founded in 2015 by the Georgian Down Syndrome Association, where young people with Down syndrome train and work beside professional artists in woodwork, ceramics and painting, and whose sales help fund the programme; 26 young people take part and more than 57 are waiting.

items.name: Kodala
items.text: A social enterprise working since 2016 that mainly employs people with disabilities to make about 200 kinds of environmentally friendly wooden toys, decorations and children’s furniture; in March 2025 its founder reported demand up by about 35% in a year.

items.name: Peacock (Parshevangi)
items.text: A social enterprise founded in Kutaisi in 2014 by the Education Development and Employment Center to bring people with disabilities into work; its 11 regular staff, and up to 15 at peak times, make quilled greeting cards, souvenirs and materials for inclusive education.
